Kāṅgri Gurukula
------------------------------------------
It is एदुचतिओन् that moulds the minds of the young ones and ultimately shapes a nation. Realising the importance of imparting basic Hindu values of life to our children even from a young age, the leaders of the आर्यसमाज् (See ĀRYA SAMĀJ also.) started a गुरुकुल type (See GURUKULA.) of institution in A.
in Punjab. What started as an experimental primary school, gradually developed into a big educational complex and was shifted to Kāṇgri near Hardwar (in Uttaranchal) in A.
. It was given the status of a deemed university in A.

.
The institution is entirely residential and is modelled on the ancient गुरुकुल system. Hindi is the medium of instruction even at the post-graduate level though Sanskrit is given a prominent place. There are separate sections for boys and girls. No distinction is made based on caste, region, social or economic status. All are given the same facilities and treated alike. The subjects taught include Sanskrit, Hindi, mathematics, geography, history, drawing, धर्मशास्त्रस्, एथिच्स् as also some basic training in a few trades like weaving mats. In higher classes English and science are also taught.
Vedamahāvidyālaya and आयुर्वेद-mahāvidyālaya are its two wings at the graduate and post-graduate levels.

kaṅkaṇa
(‘that which expresses auspiciousness’)
------------------------------------------
Images of Hindu gods and goddesses including the minor deities are often shown with several ornaments. One such is the कङ्कण (bangle, bracelet). The number varies from two to seven on each hand. The material used may be gold (suvarṇa) or conch-shell studded with pearls (maṇi-कङ्कण).
A कङ्कण may be round (valaya) or like a lotus-stem (mṛṇālavalaya).
It is said to signify auspiciousness (kam = śubha or auspiciousness; kaṇa = to produce by sound).
